scope: Repository language integration map and deferred audit scope across mobile, web, backend, public marketing and external surfaces. Read-only source inventory; no app or runtime changes.

TABLES contains en/fa only; LocaleCode follows its keys. pickLocale() at 3917–3923 maps fa/prs to fa and every other device language, including ps, to en. Reviewed Pashto copy must be registered and detection explicitly extended before enabling it.

initLocaleFromPref reads locale_pref from app_meta but accepts only en/fa at 3976. setLocale at 3995 publishes runtime changes to subscribers. Invalid/missing preferences fall back to device detection. Keep this bootstrap sequencing and preference behavior consistent when ps is introduced.
ShareLangPref is auto/ask/LocaleCode; getShareLangPref at 4012–4019 accepts only ask/en/fa. Message language can differ from app UI language; resolveShareLang at 4023 follows the app only for auto.

tIn uses the selected locale table, then English fallback, and replaces every occurrence of named placeholders via replaceAll. Translation validation must retain exact placeholder names and multiplicity. isPlaceholderSelfName at 4053–4057 explicitly compares only English/Dari restore names and also needs ps coverage.

Locale initialization runs in the asynchronous boot gate before rendering. At 582–583 device-language detection recognizes fa/prs only; this feeds onboarding routing. Client check-in reports separate device_locale and app_locale at 1851–1858.

Default onboarding path skips the language choice only when deviceIsPersian is true. The boolean is produced in app/_layout.tsx:583 and app/onboarding/index.tsx:20. Decide the intended flow for recognized Pashto devices rather than treating ps as an unrecognized locale.

Picker accepts only en/fa; cards iterate those values at 71 and hardcode self-names English/دری in visual and accessibility labels at 77/87. Persisted locale_pref is written at 46 before advancing. Add a separate پښتو option after copy review.

LANGUAGE_OPTIONS lists system/en/fa; MESSAGE_LANGUAGE_OPTIONS at 101 lists auto/ask/en/fa. Stored locale_pref filtering at 273–274 accepts only en/fa. Preference writes are at 469 and 502; actual option sheets render at 931–979.

Account calendar preview duplicates the automatic fa→jalali / other→gregorian rule; punctuation checks exact fa at 561. Qamari preview formats the active locale at 962. Review desired Pashto calendar default and separators independently from text translation.
The person-page outgoing-message language sheet explicitly offers fa and en only. It feeds sharing/export flows that may use a locale different from the active UI.
The member-invitation share-language sheet explicitly offers fa and en only. Labels use main i18n catalog keys.
Shared-account link dialog iterates only fa/en when asking a message language and maps the labels with an exact fa conditional at 198. It composes the outgoing invite with tIn(language, ...) at 130.

Shared-ledger upload stores args.lang as snapshot.locale; the receiver-facing web/SSR shell follows that message locale. The app calendar preference is sent independently. Translated generated entry notes may be baked into shared snapshots; preserve user-entered notes and names.
deriveDir returns RTL only for exact fa. useIsRTL subscribes to locale changes, so this affects text alignment, row direction and script-safe letter spacing across the app. Include ps when approved.

I18nManager is intentionally neutralized with allowRTL(false), swapLeftAndRightInRTL(false), and a one-time forceRTL(false) migration at 98–102. App-controlled RTL is separate from native Yoga direction; do not re-enable process-global RTL as a translation shortcut.

All sans weights use bundled Vazirmatn; Inter and JetBrains Mono aliases are also available. Family choice is no longer locale-specific. Pashto glyph coverage, joining, diacritics, bold weights and iOS clipping need visual verification before rollout; text extraction cannot establish correct shaping.

Automatic calendar selects jalali only for exact fa and gregorian otherwise. Calendar preference is separate from language. Decide whether Pashto should use jalali automatically; do not change persisted explicit calendar choices.

AFGHAN_MONTHS and AFGHAN_MONTHS_LATIN, GREGORIAN_MONTHS_EN/FA and QAMARI_MONTHS_EN/FA store 36 English/Dari month pairs outside the catalog. Date formatting at 317–322 is typed en/fa and chooses Persian-script names/digits only for fa. Draft month rows are in mobile extra review records.

Week begins Saturday for fa or any non-Gregorian calendar, otherwise Monday. Day numbers use faDigits only for fa at 116; weekday labels are dynamic main-catalog keys at 89. Review Pashto week-start/digit conventions.
Week-start rule duplicates CalendarDayPicker; calendar day numbers use faDigits only for exact fa at 362. Weekday/preset text is obtained through dynamic catalog keys at 252/330.
Clock digits use faDigits only for fa and separators use exact fa at 47; AM/PM are catalog keys. formatCalendarDate at 30 uses the active locale plus separate effective-calendar preference.

Weekday names come from Intl.DateTimeFormat using fa-AF for fa and en otherwise. Digits and joining punctuation at 17/28/41/44–45 have the same two-language branch. A Pashto table alone would leave reminder weekdays/numbers English.
formatFilterClock and date-label helper are typed en/fa at 127/139; faDigits and separators branch only on fa at 131/148.
toAsciiDigits accepts Extended Arabic-Indic and Arabic-Indic digits before ASCII-only validation. Keep input normalization intact when adjusting Pashto display digits.

Amounts intentionally format whole-number grouping with en-US, independent of UI language. Input normalizes localized decimal/digit variants at 9–20. This is a product formatting decision requiring review rather than automatic translation.
CURRENCIES has 9 English/Dari display-name pairs. getCurrencyName at 72 branches only on fa. ISO codes and symbols are stable identifiers; draft Pashto names are separate extra review records.

COUNTRIES has 11 English-only names. CountryPickerSheet.tsx:54 filters raw English c.name and :136 renders it; account.tsx:856 also displays prefC.name. Translate display/search names together while retaining ISO codes, flags and dial codes.

compareCustomerNames and customer-filter options are typed en/fa. Name text chunks use localeCompare with that locale at 138. A Pashto rollout should exercise sorting with Pashto names and mixed local/Latin digits.

Search strips combining marks and normalizes Arabic/Persian Yeh/Kaf forms without rewriting stored names. Verify Pashto keyboard/spelling behavior before expanding normalization; preserve meaningful Pashto letters.

Note search has its own normalization, Persian/Arabic letter handling and an afn/؋/افغانی currency-only query exclusion at 34. TallySearchOptions is en/fa at 36. Review Pashto currency spelling and note-search behavior without changing stored notes.

Notification review action categories are registered only for en/fa; buttons use tIn(locale, tab.accept/reject). Push registration passes active locale at 228 and category IDs include getLocale at 341. Extend native category registration and backend push-language handling together.
Inbox caches are keyed by account plus getLocale. Locale is sent through fetchInbox; lib/tabs/api.ts:320–323 accepts a locale query parameter. Preserve locale-specific caching when ps is enabled.

Sign-up/reset APIs accept language strings and forward them to backend email paths. Verification/reset at 1373–1396 and password setup/change/removal at 1887–1964 also pass lang. UI sends getLocale from EmailAuthFlow.tsx:342/363/376/397 and account-password.tsx:254/286/305. Backend templates must support ps alongside the mobile rollout.

PDF HTML language/direction choose RTL only for fa at 131; prose counts and record detail functions are typed en/fa at 103/336. CSV labels use tIn with export locale (csv.ts:82 onward). Data snapshots use LocaleCode independently of message and calendar settings. Review layout, glyphs, columns and CSV consumers after approved copy is applied.

Boot splash and migration/recovery prompts render hardcoded English and Dari together through 1625 because locale preferences may be inaccessible. English-only backup failures at 1302–1309/1372 and backup-age text at 1528–1531 are included in extra review rows. Future Pashto recovery must remain usable before database or fonts load.

Expo contactsPermission is configured in English at 63; cameraPermission in English at 77. Native permission messages need build-time localization and OS testing; changing runtime i18n tables does not localize them.

Live cloud-sync background notification channel name/description and message title/body are hardcoded English at 73–75/111–117. Despite its mesh directory this path is active for cloud-origin ledger changes. Extra review rows include all 5 English messages.

Native defaults Nearby sync is on / Tap to open Kaata / Nearby sync are English at 109–111. Notification reads persisted title/body and channel values at 540–542/577–579. JavaScript supplies translated fgs catalog values in lib/mesh/foreground.ts:53–55/86–89; maintain a safe localized fallback if the feature is re-enabled.

Release notes and announcement title/body/CTA label are loaded as server-supplied strings, persisted at 71–81, and displayed verbatim in components/UpdateBanner.tsx:40–45/86–107. Client has no locale-specific table selection for these payloads. Repository-only catalog extraction cannot capture active stored content.
DEVICE_PREF_KEYS preserves locale_pref and calendar_pref during start-fresh account switching. Include ps in accepted locale values while retaining language/calendar preferences across this flow.
